findings.statement: The filing reports that the gross margin percentage decreased three basis points in 2026 (11.09% against 11.12% in 2025), the opposite of a noticeable widening.
findings.rationale: The gross margin table and the MD&A text both show a small decline in the headline gross margin percentage, so the overall markup did not widen.

quotes.text: Gross margin percentage decreased three basis points.

findings.statement: Excluding gasoline price inflation, the gross margin percentage was 11.22%, an increase of 10 basis points, which is modest and driven by mix rather than a broad widening of markup.
findings.rationale: Adjusted for gasoline, the margin rose slightly, so the claim has some partial support. The filing attributes the increase to warehouse ancillary and other businesses, offset by a decrease in core merchandise categories, and describes the change as sales mix, so it is not evidence of a noticeable widening in merchandise markup.

quotes.text: Excluding the impact of gasoline price inflation on net sales, gross margin percentage was 11.22%, an increase of 10 basis points.

findings.statement: Within core merchandise categories, gross margin as a percentage of their own sales increased 15 basis points, while warehouse ancillary and other businesses decreased 14 basis points.
findings.rationale: This is the closest measure to merchandise markup in the passages and it did rise, but by a small amount, and the filing's own total moved the other way. Whether 15 basis points is noticeable is a judgement the passages do not settle.

quotes.text: The gross margin in core merchandise categories when expressed as a percentage of their own sales increased 15 basis points.
Gross margin in warehouse ancillary and other businesses when expressed as a percentage of their own sales decreased 14 basis points, primarily due to gasoline and pharmacy.

findings.statement: The backend-computed annual gross margin was 12.8% in the fiscal year ended 2026-08-30 and 12.8% in the prior fiscal year, which shows no widening on that measure.
findings.rationale: The figures are identical across the two years, but they use a different definition from the filing's 11.09% and 11.12%, so they are weaker evidence than the filing's own table.

response.rationale: The filing's headline gross margin percentage edged down, and the backend annual gross margin figures are flat. Only the core merchandise categories and the gasoline-adjusted view show small increases, and the filing explains the movements mostly by sales mix. The passages do not support a noticeably wider markup.
unknowns: Whether the thesis means total gross margin or core merchandise markup, which the passages report differently.
Why the backend gross margin figures (12.8%) differ from the filing's gross margin percentage; the definitions are not given in the passages.
What size of change the analyst would count as noticeable.
